sources.title: John B. Schneider, Understanding the Finite-Difference Time-Domain Method
sources.locator: Full 415-page author-hosted PDF. Chapter 2 §§2.8–2.14 for field equations, conductivity, PEC and boundary conventions; Chapter 3 §§3.2–3.3 and §3.12 for staggered updates and conductivity; Chapter 5 §§5.7–5.8 for conductivity and planar-interface transmission; Chapter 7 §7.4 for dispersion; Chapter 8 §8.8 for PEC grid treatment; Chapter 9 §§9.3 and 9.7 for the 3D Yee grid and unequal spacings.
sources.reading_status: The complete book PDF was downloaded and its 415-page extent verified. The cited sections were extracted and read in full. The text extractor emitted syntax warnings on unrelated pages; the cited sections were inspected in the extracted text. No 3D closed-form dispersion claim is imported from the book.

read_evidence.extent: 415 PDF pages; complete PDF downloaded, with detailed reading of the cited Maxwell/FDTD sections.

sources.support: Maxwell material/boundary conventions, Yee staggering and centered conductivity, the 1D dispersion derivation, 3D grid placement, PEC grid modeling, and planar dielectric transmission context. All claims beyond those exact source statements are derived locally.

contents.name: Maxwell field equations, material conductivity and PEC conventions
contents.detail: Chapter 2 §§2.8–2.14 support the real-field, PEC and conductivity conventions. The local definition supplies the precise tensor, distributional and interface hypotheses.

contents.name: Staggered Yee grid, curl updates and centered conductivity treatment
contents.detail: Chapter 3 §§3.2–3.3, §3.12 and Chapter 9 §9.3 support the staggered placement and update convention; the local matrix rows are stated explicitly.

contents.name: Discrete Yee energy and conductivity loss sign
contents.detail: Chapter 3 §3.12 and Chapter 5 §5.7 motivate the centered conductivity treatment; the energy identity and sign are proved locally.

contents.name: One-dimensional Yee dispersion and three-dimensional staggered grid locations
contents.detail: Chapter 7 §7.4 gives the 1D relation and explicitly cautions that its 2D/3D extension has no closed form there; Chapters 9 §§9.3 and 9.7 fix the 3D grid conventions. The 3D symbol and exact finite-grid maximum are derived locally.

contents.name: PEC field closure and staircase boundary caveat
contents.detail: Chapter 8 §8.8 describes zeroing tangential electric nodes and notes staircasing for curved boundaries. The local PEC convention is an oriented cochain closure and is justified independently.

contents.name: Planar dielectric reflection/transmission context
contents.detail: Chapter 5 §5.8 treats transmission at a planar dielectric interface. The local example directly solves the tangential trace equations for both amplitudes.

recovery_attempts.outcome: Author-hosted complete PDF downloaded; 415 pages verified with mutool.

sources.title: Long Chen, Finite Element Methods for Maxwell Equations, lecture notes
sources.locator: Complete 10-page PDF read page by page. §§1.1–1.3, printed pp. 1–6: lowest-order Nedelec and RT0 spaces, oriented degrees of freedom, commuting moments and smooth interpolation; §2, pp. 6–8: Maxwell curl-energy form and edge-element mass matrices; §3, pp. 8–10: finite element de Rham context.
sources.reading_status: The complete 10-page lecture note was downloaded and read page by page. Its assumed quasi-interpolation construction is not treated as a complete proof; the local carriers supply explicit finite-dimensional and smooth-input arguments.
sources.support: Lowest-order edge/face finite element spaces, degrees of freedom, commuting moment identities and Maxwell curl-energy context. The semidiscrete ODE and transient error estimate are proved locally.

contents.name: Lowest-order Nedelec edge fields, RT0 face fields and oriented moments
contents.detail: §§1.1–1.2 identify the edge and face spaces and their moments; the batch definition fixes its own real basis and matrix conventions.

contents.name: Smooth canonical edge and face interpolation estimates
contents.detail: §§1.1–1.3 support the smooth-input commuting and first-order estimate route. The full local scaling proof is written in the item.

contents.name: Maxwell curl-energy Ritz form and finite-dimensional orthogonality
contents.detail: §2 supplies the form context. The finite-dimensional well-definedness and best-approximation argument is proved locally.

contents.name: Finite-dimensional edge-element Maxwell energy pairing
contents.detail: §2 supplies the weighted curl-pairing context; the time-dependent matrix cancellation is derived explicitly in the item.

sources.title: Douglas N. Arnold, Richard S. Falk, and Ragnar Winther, Finite element exterior calculus: from Hodge theory to numerical stability
sources.locator: Complete 70-page article inspected. §§3.3–3.6, printed pp. 22–36: cochain projections, discrete Poincare and harmonic forms; §§5.1–5.6, printed pp. 49–59: finite element differential forms, lowest Whitney spaces, canonical interpolation limits, smoothed projection outline and cohomology.
sources.reading_status: The complete 70-page PDF was downloaded and its cited sections were read. Section 5.5 explicitly only outlines the smoothed projection construction; no uniform estimates, invertibility or boundary correction are claimed from that outline.

read_evidence.extent: 70 PDF pages; complete article inspected, with detailed reading of printed pp. 22–36 and 49–59.

sources.support: Whitney spaces and their degrees of freedom, the abstract cochain-projection framework, and the explicit limits of the source’s canonical interpolation and smoothed projection outline. The repository now has a local draft projection proof chain, but its new suppliers lack Step 1 records; the source outline is not used as proof.

contents.name: Lowest-order Whitney spaces as a finite element de Rham subcomplex
contents.detail: §§5.1–5.3 give the FEEC and lowest-order space context; concrete local functions and moment assembly are stated in the assigned items.

contents.name: Abstract bounded cochain projection properties used by the conditional initial-data construction
contents.detail: §3.3 supplies the abstract projection framework. The actual Batch 38 theorem statement is used only as a conditional interface and remains escalated because §5.5 is an outline.

contents.name: Uniform smoothed projection bounds, finite-element invertibility and zero-tangential boundary correction
contents.reason: Section 5.5 only sketches the smoothed projection and refers elsewhere; it does not establish these bounds. The run now has separate local draft proof suppliers, but their Step 1 records are absent, so no completed proof is imported from this source.

contents.name: Canonical lowest-order moments require smooth inputs
contents.detail: §5.4 warns that canonical lower-dimensional moments are not bounded on the full graph spaces; the local lemma explicitly limits itself to smooth inputs.
